Ray Dalio Says All Creativity Is 'Trapped' In Your Subconscious— and the Practice He's Used Since 1968 Is the Key to Unlocking It
data.description:
Billionaire investor Ray Dalio said decades of this one habit helped unlock creativity he believes sits "trapped" in the subconscious, giving him calm and mental clarity that he says played a decisive role in his investment career and success.

Dalio Credits Meditation With Creative Clarity

"I’ve been practicing meditation for a long time, and it has easily been one of the most powerful things that’s helped me in my life," the Bridgewater Associates founder wrote on X earlier this week. Dalio said meditation provides "an equanimity—almost like being a ninja," helping him respond calmly to challenges.

Ray Dalio
@RayDalio

I’ve been practicing meditation for a long time, and it has easily been one of the most powerful things that’s helped me in my life.

It provides an equanimity—almost like being a ninja. Everything slows down around you, and you are able to deal with whatever comes at you from a… pic.twitter.com/xvRtUjZapv

Aug 04, 2026

Dalio said meditation opens "a connection between your conscious brain and your subconscious brain," adding, "That is where the magic is, because that is where all creativity is trapped." Quieting the mind, he said, helps people "open up that channel."

Read Also: Ray Dalio Revealed Struggling To Hit The Books: His Mom Sent Him To His Room Because 'I Hated School … I Wouldn't Study' — Now He's A Billionaire

Dalio began practicing Transcendental Meditation in 1968 and has previously said, "Whatever success I’ve had in life has been more due to my meditating than anything else." His comments complement his broader philosophy of reflection, learning and systematic decision-making.

Dalio built Bridgewater from an operation launched in his New York apartment in 1975 into a hedge-fund giant. The firm managed about $102 billion in July, after Dalio sold his remaining ownership stake and left its board in 2025.

Research Shows Mixed Results On Creativity

Research offers some support for meditation’s cognitive benefits, though findings remain mixed. A National Library of Medicine-indexed randomized study published in 2014 found seven days of integrative body-mind training improved divergent-thinking creativity compared with relaxation training. A later randomized study found no significant creativity advantage from open-monitoring meditation.

Business Leaders Also Turn To Meditation

Dalio is not alone among prominent business figures who use the practice. Block Inc. (NYSE:XYZ) CEO Jack Dorsey has maintained an intensive meditation routine, while Oprah Winfrey has long made meditation part of her mornings. Virgin Group’s Richard Branson has also incorporated meditation into his routine.

Dalio’s comments go further than praising stress reduction. "If you ask me if I would be at the same level of success without it all these years," he wrote, "I don’t believe I’d be close."

US Senate to vote on advancing CLARITY Act in September after Thune files cloture
data.description:
US Senate Majority Leader John Thune has filed cloture on a motion to take up the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, also known as the CLARITY Act, setting up a key procedural vote on the crypto market structure bill for Sept. 15.

The vote is expected after the Senate reconvenes at 2:15 pm ET on Sept. 15, giving lawmakers several more weeks to work through unresolved disagreements over the legislation.

The Senate Daily Press confirmed that Thune filed cloture on the motion to bring the CLARITY Act to the Senate floor for consideration. Invoking cloture on the motion requires 60 votes, meaning Republicans will need Democratic support to clear the procedural hurdle and move toward consideration of the bill.

Thune’s move puts the CLARITY Act on a path toward Senate consideration after lawmakers failed to reach an agreement before the August recess. Negotiations have been complicated by disagreements over ethics provisions and rules governing stablecoin rewards, among other issues.

Source: Eleanor Terrett

While the move marks progress for the legislation, it does not guarantee that the CLARITY Act will receive a final vote or pass the Senate. The cloture vote concerns whether to take up the legislation for consideration, rather than passage of the bill itself.

The CLARITY Act is considered a landmark piece of US crypto legislation that would establish a federal market structure for digital assets, clarify when crypto assets fall under securities or commodities laws and delineate oversight responsibilities between the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

Until now, negotiations have stalled over proposed ethics provisions that would restrict government officials and their families from issuing or profiting from digital assets while in office.

In an effort to break that impasse, lawmakers have been reportedly working on a bipartisan ethics addendum aimed at addressing Democratic concerns over President Donald Trump’s crypto-related financial interests. As Bloomberg reported Thursday, the proposal would require the president to divest from certain crypto-related businesses.

data.title: XRP Nears $1 — How Low Could It Go This Weekend? Here's the Target
data.description:
XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) is down 2% on Friday, pressing onto the $1 psychological level with thin weekend liquidity ahead and a chart setup pointing toward $0.85.

Why $1 Is The Level That Matters This Weekend

The chart projects a 15% to 17% drop from $1 if the level fails on a daily or weekly close, with $0.85 to $0.88 as the measured move target based on the depth of the two-month compression pattern.

RSI at 34.19 sits near oversold territory but has not reached an extreme yet, meaning there is still room to fall before a technical bounce becomes likely.

Weekend volume is thin, and breakdowns in low liquidity tend to overshoot rather than find clean support.

What ETF Flows Are Showing

XRP ETF inflows hit just $1.01 million this week, well below the prior three weeks of $14.86 million, $8.15 million, and $6.78 million respectively according to SoSoValue.

The institutional momentum that built through July has clearly slowed heading into the weekend.

Friday’s session has yet to report its flows, but even a few million dollars in additional inflows would likely leave this week’s total well below previous weeks.

Why The Clarity Act Failed To Help

Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott (R-SC) said Thursday the Senate should hold a procedural vote on the Clarity Act before recess.

However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) held a vote on the budget resolution instead, with no cloture filing on the Clarity Act confirmed at publication time.

XRP fell further on the news, with regulatory clarity remaining one of the token’s key narrative drivers.

What The Derivatives Data Is Showing?

Volume jumped 16.52% to $2.52 billion Friday as traders pile in around the $1 level according to Coinglass. Nearly everyone is still positioned for a bounce, with long/short ratios at 3.0 on Binance, 3.7 on OKX, and 3.57 among top traders.

The problem is the longs keep losing. Long liquidations hit $11.75 million in 24 hours against just $310,000 in shorts.

Shorts are barely touched while bulls absorb hit after hit. Open interest dipped slightly to $2.34 billion as some traders finally gave up and closed positions.

With most traders still long into a falling price at the most critical level on the chart, a $1.00 break could force a wave of selling that pushes XRP lower faster than the chart target alone suggests.

Image: Shutterstock

data.title: Benzinga's 'Stock Whisper' Index: 5 Stocks Investors Secretly Monitor But Don't Talk About Yet
data.description:
Each week, Benzinga’s Stock Whisper Index uses a combination of proprietary data and pattern recognition to showcase five stocks that are just under the surface and deserve attention.

Investors are constantly on the hunt for undervalued, under-followed and emerging stocks. With countless methods available to retail traders, the challenge often lies in sifting through the abundance of information to uncover new opportunities and understand why certain stocks should be of interest.

Here’s a look at the Benzinga Stock Whisper Index for the week ending August 7:

Lucid Group (NASDAQ:LCID): The electric vehicle company saw elevated interest this week with two main news items helping put attention on the stock. The company saw Prince Al Waleed bin Talal Al Saud disclose a 19,513,000 shares passive stake in the company. The stake adds to the company already being well-financed by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund and could show signs of support for a turnaround of the company and future growth. Lucid also reported second-quarter financial results. Revenue was up 56% year-over-year, but fell shy of analyst estimates. The company’s quarterly loss per share also missed a Street estimate. Lucid is focused on robotaxis and midsize vehicles going forward. The stock continues to be one of the most watched from retail traders and is also one of the most-shorted stocks, which puts more attention on shares anytime the stock is volatile or has major news.

Jersey Mike’s Subs (NYSE:JMKE): The sandwich chain is one of the newest public companies completing its IPO on July 30. The company went public with shares priced at $23. The stock opened for trading at $21 and over a week later shares trade at around $23. Investors focused on the long-term could consider the companies ambitious goals of 5,000 or more U.S. stores and 15,000 global locations. While hot IPOs that see shares soar after listing can be good for early investors and early IPO backers, the listings that see the stock trade near the IPO price after the debut give investors more opportunities to get in at the same price as those who backed the offering.

Rigetti Computing (NASDAQ:RGTI): The quantum computing stock has fallen out of favor for some time, but was back in the spotlight with quarterly financial results and positive commentary on the sector by IBM’s CEO. The company reported mixed earnings with earnings per share in-line with analyst estimates and revenue narrowly missing Street targets. Rigetti said it is focused on its "core technology roadmap" moving forward and is seeing strong engagement across multiple sectors of customers. Rigetti stock was up around 18% over the last week, while shares remain down over 25% year-to-date in 2026.

Serve Robotics (NASDAQ:SERV): Shares of Serve fell after the company reported second-quarter results that missed estimates and the company cut its guidance. Revenue of $3.28 million missed a Street estimate of $3.49 million, while the company beat estimates for earnings per share. Going forward Serve is focused on partnerships, more diversified revenue streams and new monetization opportunities. The company’s new guidance is for full-year revenue of $9 million to $10 million, significantly lower than a previous guide of $26 million. With robotics remaining a key investment theme, the stock remains one to watch, but will likely need to turn in a great quarter or two or have major news to get investors excited once again.

Joby Aviation (NYSE:JOBY): Shares of the electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) company were volatile during the week with multiple news pieces to keep investors engaged in the stock. The company announced a multi-year agreement with Virgin Atlantic for its official U.K. airline partner. The deal will include multiple U.K. routes going forward. Joby reported second-quarter financial results on Wednesday with earnings per share missing Street estimates and revenue coming in higher than estimates. The company raised its full year revenue guidance after the results. Joby also announced a new lease at Perot Field Fort Worth Alliance Airport, which gives the company a presence in Texas. While Joby shares were up nearly 20% over the last five trading days, the stock is down 40% year-to-date. The eVTOL stock could be one to watch and belongs to a sector that will likely continued to be talked about for high growth going forward.

Stay tuned for next week’s report, and follow Benzinga Pro for all the latest headlines and top market-moving stories here.

data.title: Bitcoin, ether ETFs draw $1.1 billion in best inflow week since April, despite low volume
data.description:
U.S. spot bitcoin and ether ETFs saw a combined $1.1 billion in inflows last week, the strongest week for either category since April, per The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data.

The spot bitcoin (BTC) ETFs took in about $853.5 million, their largest weekly total since the week ending April 17, which saw $996.4 million in inflows, per the data. Spot ether ETFs saw $244.9 million in inflows, likewise their best result since the very same week.

Last week, bitcoin ETFs recorded inflows in all five sessions, led by $244.4 million in inflows Wednesday and $211.5 million on Tuesday. Thursday and Friday saw $128.7 million and $98.9 million, respectively.

BlackRock's IBIT fund accounted for $693.7 million of the total BTC fund inflows, or more than 80% of the total. Fidelity's FBTC accounted for 13% of the total inflows, with $116.4 million, making the two largest bitcoin funds by assets under management the most significant gainers on the week.

Coldcard exploit connection?

Eric Balchunas, senior ETF analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said in an X post Friday that BlackRock's IBIT, Fidelity's FBTC and several other funds have drawn inflows every day since the Coldcard hack, making it "hard not to see causation in the correlation."

"Would be ironic, but somehow on brand, if the hack of btc in cold storage (seemingly worst [possible] situation) marked the beginning of next run," Balchunas wrote.

The exploit, which surfaced July 30, has led to at least $111 million in thefts and estimated total losses could exceed $130 million, Galaxy Research said Friday.

OKX told The Block last week that the exploit drove record inflows to centralized exchanges, and research and brokerage firm K33 measured about 890,000 BTC moving onchain over seven days, a 2026 high.

Countering the Coldcard narrative, however, ether ETFs posted their own best week since April over the same five sessions, despite the fact that ether holders have no exposure to a Bitcoin-only hardware wallet vulnerability.

The category's inflow run also began on Aug. 3, several days after the vulnerability was first disclosed. Bitcoin rose about 3% on the week and touched an August high above $65,300 on Friday, when U.S. payrolls fell by 23,000 against forecasts for an 80,000 gain and traders priced out a September rate hike, The Block previously reported. Most of the week's buying preceded that release, as the two sessions after it saw the weakest inflows of the five.

Ether funds extend positive run to five weeks

Spot ether (ETH) ETFs have logged five consecutive positive weeks, their longest run of 2026, per SoSoValue data. Thursday produced the largest daily gain at $92.2 million in inflows, while Monday's $11.4 million outflow was the only negative session.

The funds held $10.74 billion in net assets Friday against $11.46 billion in cumulative net inflows, leaving them about $711 million underwater on a mark-to-market basis. That gap has narrowed from roughly $2.0 billion in mid-June.

Whales, meanwhile, are aggressively accumulating ETH, CryptoQuant said in a recent report. Wallets holding between 10,000 and 100,000 ETH have increased their balances to a record 19.6 million ETH from about 14 million ETH in mid-2025, per the report.

Volume remains near multi-year lows

Bitcoin ETF trading volume totaled to about $8.19 billion on the week, down 9% from the previous week's $9.02 billion. That's the second-lowest full trading week since October 2024; only the week ending July 24 had lower volume with $8.05 billion. Ether ETF volume came to roughly $2.38 billion, down about 21% from the prior week.

The rebound has also not erased the funds' overall losses for 2026. Bitcoin ETFs remain at approximately $4.44 billion in net outflows since the start of the year, while ether ETFs are down roughly $873 million.

Bitcoin traded near $65,100 on Saturday morning, while ether changed hands around $1,920, according to The Block's Bitcoin and Ethereum price pages.

XRP Ledger Launches Six-Amendment Vote, Unveils Major v3.3.0 Upgrade With Confidential Transfers and Institutional Tools
data.description:
The proposals include Confidential Transfer, Batch, Permission Delegation, Sponsor, Dynamic MPT, and a bundled cleanup amendment. None of these features should be considered active on the XRP Ledger yet. Under the network's amendment process, a proposal must maintain more than 80% validator support for two consecutive weeks before it can activate.

The release follows several months of development work around the next generation of XRP Ledger functionality. Development activity shows support being added across the XRPL software ecosystem for features including Batch V1.1, Dynamic MPT, and the new cleanup amendment ahead of the 3.3.0 release.

XRPL validator Vet described the package as a major release, highlighting privacy, transaction batching, sponsored fees, delegated permissions, and token flexibility among the changes heading into the voting process.

Privacy and transaction upgrades lead the proposal

Confidential Transfer is the most notable privacy-focused proposal in the XRP Ledger v3.3.0 package. According to the official XRPL amendment documentation, the feature is designed to provide institutional-grade privacy for Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTs) using EC-ElGamal encryption and zero-knowledge proofs.

XRP Ledger v3.3.0 has launched with six proposed amendments now open for validator voting. Source: XRP Ledger Operations via X

The proposed system would shield individual MPT balances and transfer amounts from public view while retaining mechanisms that allow authorized parties, such as issuers or auditors, to verify relevant information. This distinction is important for institutional use cases, where transaction confidentiality may need to coexist with reporting and regulatory requirements.

The Batch amendment addresses a different limitation by allowing multiple transactions to be executed as a single atomic operation. The updated Batch V1.1 implementation has also been incorporated into XRPL developer tooling, including xrpl4j, as work progressed toward the 3.3.0 release.

Atomic execution means the transactions in a batch are treated as one coordinated operation rather than a series of independent actions. That can be useful for more complex settlement flows, including transactions that need several steps to succeed together.

Permission Delegation is aimed at account management and institutional security. The feature allows an account owner to assign specific transaction permissions to another account without handing over control of the primary account's keys.

The approach can separate operational duties from asset custody. For example, an organization could maintain assets in a more secure account while allowing another wallet to perform narrowly defined transactions. The proposal is also a revised version of an earlier Permission Delegation implementation. XRPL developers previously disabled that version after a vulnerability was identified, with PermissionDelegationV1_1 developed as its replacement.

Sponsor introduces another change that could affect how applications interact with the XRP Ledger. It allows one account to cover transaction fees and reserve requirements for another account under defined conditions.

For developers, sponsored costs could make applications easier to use because newcomers would not necessarily need to manage XRP for every initial network interaction. The underlying goal is to reduce friction around account funding and transaction execution.

@Vet_X0, an XRP Ledger validator, calls XRPL v3.3.0 a major release featuring the network’s first native privacy amendment for encrypted MPT balances and transfers. Source: @Vet_X0 via X

Dynamic MPT, meanwhile, focuses on token issuers. The amendment is associated with XLS-94 and is designed to make selected properties of Multi-Purpose Tokens changeable after issuance. That gives issuers additional flexibility when managing tokenized assets whose operational requirements can evolve over time. XRPL documentation currently lists DynamicMPT as an amendment in development.

The sixth proposal, FixCleanup, groups technical fixes intended to improve protocol stability and address issues within the XRP Ledger's implementation.

Together, the amendments cover several different layers of the network. Confidential Transfer focuses on privacy, Batch on transaction composition, Permission Delegation on account control, Sponsor on user experience, and Dynamic MPT on token management.

Performance improvements now await validator approval

The 3.3.0 release also includes infrastructure work intended to improve the experience of running XRP Ledger nodes. Development updates have highlighted efforts to reduce resource requirements and improve synchronization for node operators.

XRPL v3.3.0 introduces Confidential Transfers, using EC-ElGamal encryption and zero-knowledge proofs to shield MPT balances and transfer amounts while preserving cryptographic verifiability. Source: @iamalijandro via X

Earlier reports based on Vet's development updates cited potential memory reductions ranging from roughly 10% to as much as 40% in certain conditions. The more conservative figures associated with the current release indicate memory usage reductions of around 10% to 15%. The exact benefit can vary depending on the node's workload and environment.

Lower resource consumption matters because validators and other node operators must continuously maintain and synchronize ledger data. Improvements in memory efficiency and synchronization can reduce the infrastructure burden associated with operating the network.

The upgrade also reflects the iterative nature of XRP Ledger development. Several components in version 3.3.0 have undergone revisions before reaching the validator stage. Batch and Permission Delegation, in particular, have previously required changes following security reviews and subsequent development work.

The validator vote is therefore the next critical step rather than the final confirmation that the features will become part of the live protocol.

Each amendment must maintain the required supermajority for two consecutive weeks before activation. XRPL's official documentation states that amendments that meet this threshold can become enabled on the mainnet, while proposals that fail to sustain sufficient support do not activate.

If the six proposals clear that process, the XRP Ledger would gain a broader set of native tools for confidential token transfers, atomic transactions, delegated account permissions, sponsored costs, and flexible MPT management.

For institutions exploring tokenized assets, the combination is particularly relevant because it addresses several practical requirements at once: privacy, controlled access, transaction coordination, and token administration. However, the significance of the upgrade will ultimately depend on validator approval and subsequent adoption by developers and network participants.

Lithium Price Analysis: Carbonate Holds 142,750 Yuan After Recent Pullback
data.description:
Battery material has seen a modest correction in the past session, adding 1,250yuan or 0.88%, as the overall trend leans toward consolidation after a robust first-half rally. Battery-grade lithium carbonate prices have been volatile as supply and demand fundamentals change across the market.

Lithium Price Finds Support After Lengthy Pullback

The 1-year chart of lithium carbonate illustrates a healthy rebound from late 2025 levels before a correction ensues. Prices increased rapidly in the first few months of 2026 before reaching the levels of almost 200,000 yuan/tonne in May and then easing back to the present 142,750 level.

The diagram shows that LIT is finding a higher band than its 2025 lows. Following the May peak, prices retraced through June and July to create a downward trend. The recent advance towards 142,750yuan reflects the market testing a support zone after falling away from the previous rally.

Today’s daily movement: 0.88% higher as lithium carbonate rebounds from the recent sideways trading sessions. Price has been trading inside a narrow price band near recent lows, indicating lower price volatility relative to the drastic range trading seen earlier in the year.

The short-term structure has resistance building in the 150,000-160,000 yuan area. Above this zone, it would be a greater correction, whereas if it remains weak, it would be targeted towards a lower support area.

Lithium Carbonate Technical Indicators Show Neutral Momentum

Meanwhile, the TradingView chart for other lithium-related assets appears to have a neutral technical setup. The MACD indicator moved to the middle after previous buying momentum weakened. The latest values read MACD 0.01 and histogram -0.08.

This is a sign that the momentum is slowing down after the recent push. The directional indicator is not showing a strong directional movement.

However, the RSI is at about 49.75. The RSI is still at the moderate 50 levels and remains somewhat away from its earlier heavy values, signaling that lithium is no longer witnessing the kind of momentum it had witnessed in the previous rally.

The graph of the lithium stock index displayed another significant intraday move to 242.43. The stock fluctuated primarily between 235 and 238 during the session. The move was enough to take the index away from the recent lows, although momentum indicators showed signs of easing.

Lithium Market Tracks Supply And Demand Shifts

Nonetheless, the lithium carbonate market is still closely following revisions to battery demand, inventory levels, and activity in production. According to market information, lithium prices have recovered from earlier lows and are back up to levels below those seen at the 2026 high earlier this year.

Price evaluations conducted over the past three months highlight the continuing vulnerability of battery-grade lithium carbonate to supply responses to demand from the electric vehicle and energy storage markets.

What is important here, because of the current chart structure, is 142,750 yuan as short-term support. Maintaining this level preserves the recent consolidation scheme; breaking below could carry us down even further.

On the positive side, lithium carbonate has to return to the 150000 yuan level in order to restore a bullish stance in the short term. Overall, the market is still in the consolidation area between the recovery moves and the correction after the May peak.
